# Booklet

> Publish Markdown incident reports, ADRs, RFCs and runbooks as web pages, with team spaces.

Booklet publishes Markdown as a web page with a link. It is built for engineering documents: a page can carry a type, status and owners, link to other pages, and live in a team space. Publishing works from the web editor, a REST API, a CLI, a GitHub Action and an MCP server. It can be tried without an account.

## What Booklet does

- Converts Markdown into a formatted web page with a URL
- Renders GitHub-Flavored Markdown — headings, code blocks, tables, lists, task lists, blockquotes — plus KaTeX math, Mermaid and Graphviz diagrams, callouts (`> [!NOTE]`, `[!TIP]`, `[!WARNING]`, `[!IMPORTANT]`, `[!CAUTION]`), collapsible toggle sections, and multi-column layouts
- Auto-generates a table of contents once a document has enough headings
- Reads YAML frontmatter: `title`, `slug`, `visibility`, `description`, `author`, `date`, `tags`, and for engineering documents `type` (`incident`, `postmortem`, `adr`, `rfc`, `runbook`, `release-notes`), `status`, `severity`, `owners`, `supersedes`, shown in a strip above the page
- Live preview in the browser editor as you type
- Multiple named drafts, saved in the browser and synced to the account when signed in
- 21 built-in templates (incident report, ADR, runbook, release notes, postmortem, and more — full list below)
- Export a published page to Markdown or self-contained HTML; PDF through the browser's print dialog
- Per-page analytics: views, read depth, referrers (signed-in only)
- Version history: the last 50 versions of a page, with a line diff and restore (signed-in only)
- Password-protected pages (signed-in only)
- Custom URL slugs (signed-in only)
- Team spaces: a shared collection of pages under one URL (`/t/<slug>`), grouped by document type, with invited members. A page can be team-only: members can open it, everyone else gets a 404
- `[[Title]]` in a published page links to the published page of that title in the same team space (or among the author's own pages), and that page lists what references it
- New pages are unlisted (not indexed) unless the author makes them public; public pages appear on Explore, newest first
- Every published page has a "Report this page" link; a taken-down page returns 410 Gone

## REST API

All endpoints are under `/api/v1/`, authenticated with `Authorization: Bearer <bklt_...>`:

- `POST /api/v1/publish` — create a new page, returns `{ id, url }`
- `PATCH /api/v1/pages/{id}` — update an existing page in place (same URL)
- `GET /api/v1/pages` — list pages owned by the authenticated account, with `q`, `tag`, `type` and `space` filters, paged by `cursor`
- `GET /api/v1/pages/{id}` — read a page's metadata and raw Markdown
- `DELETE /api/v1/pages/{id}` — delete a page permanently

API keys are generated at /settings/api-keys after signing in (free). Errors are RFC 9457 problem details (`application/problem+json`). The OpenAPI 3.1 document is at /api/v1/openapi.json.

Full reference: https://booklet.ashwinsathian.com/api-docs

## MCP (Model Context Protocol)

Booklet runs an MCP server, so Claude and other MCP clients can publish and manage pages from a conversation.

MCP endpoint: `https://booklet-mcp.ashwinsathian.com/mcp` (remote, Streamable HTTP, protocol 2026-07-28; nothing to install)
Auth: OAuth sign-in (Claude.ai custom connectors and other clients that support it: add the URL, sign in, no key), or an `Authorization: Bearer <bklt_...>` header with the same API key as the REST API

**Tools:** `publish_page`, `update_page`, `get_page`, `list_pages`, `delete_page`, `create_document`, `search_pages`
**Resources:** the account's published pages, as `booklet://pages/:id`
**Prompts:** five document templates the assistant can fill in and publish: `incident_report`, `adr`, `release_notes`, `rfc`, `runbook`

Setup instructions (Claude Desktop, Claude.ai, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Zed): https://booklet.ashwinsathian.com/mcp-setup

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "booklet": {
      "url": "https://booklet-mcp.ashwinsathian.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## CLI

```
npx booklet-cli publish README.md
```

Or install it globally: `npm install -g booklet-cli`. Supports non-interactive auth (`--key` / `BOOKLET_API_KEY`) for CI, `--update <id>` to republish a page in place, `--watch` for auto-republish on save, and shell completion.

npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/booklet-cli

## GitHub Action

`AshwinSathian/publish-to-booklet` publishes a Markdown file to Booklet from a CI workflow and returns the URL as a step output:

```yaml
- uses: AshwinSathian/publish-to-booklet@v2
  with:
    file: CHANGELOG.md
    api-key: ${{ secrets.BOOKLET_API_KEY }}
```

Repository: https://github.com/AshwinSathian/publish-to-booklet

## Pricing

Free. There is no paid tier. Publishing without an account is capped at 10 pages per month per IP address, and those pages are kept for 90 days unless the author signs in and claims them. An account is also free: it removes the cap, its pages do not expire, and it adds custom slugs, analytics, version history, password protection, team spaces, API keys and webhooks. Every published page carries a small Booklet mark in its footer, and there is no option to remove it.

## Technical details

- Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- Self-hosted MongoDB; the app runs as a single process on one machine behind a Cloudflare Tunnel
- No user content is used for training or resold
- No third-party analytics or tracking scripts
- Open source: the app is AGPL-3.0-only; the CLI, API client, MCP server and GitHub Action are MIT
- XSS-safe: content renders through a custom block-based AST renderer, never as raw injected HTML

## Templates available

Incident Report, Architecture Decision Record (ADR), Release Notes, README, Meeting Notes, Onboarding Guide, Runbook, Postmortem, Weekly Update, Product Spec, Design Review, API Changelog, Technical Investigation, Sprint Retrospective, Job Description, Interview Debrief, Project Kickoff, Launch Checklist, Data Dictionary, Proposal, User Research Report
